selection.name: LangWatch
selection.role: C05 — Provisional sole local trace store and agent-session inspector. Narrowly preferred for its documented local bootstrap and native OpenTelemetry integration with both named clients. No second tool has a distinct, necessary job in this packet.

basis.shows: Documents the local server command with Node.js as the stated prerequisite, plus CLI integrations for Claude Code and Codex. This establishes a supported install path, not lower resource consumption.
Documents ingestion from OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation in any language into the platform's OTEL API.
Documents Claude Code trace, log and metric exporters, content-capture controls, and routing to a self-hosted instance through /api/otel.

Documents Codex native OTLP/HTTP trace and event exporters, self-hosted endpoint paths, and CLI instrumentation. The manual native export supplies metadata; conversation capture requires the additional CLI capture described by the project.

Defines packaged-install smoke tests from a fresh sandbox on Ubuntu, Ubuntu arm64 and macOS, with service-health checks and a workflow execution test. I inspected the suite definition; I did not verify a passing execution of this suite.
Defines unit, component and integration test lanes. These are public test-suite evidence, not a measured comparison against another candidate.

Includes Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 build targets for bundled dependencies. Linux support makes WSL2 Ubuntu a plausible target; an actual WSL2 installation remains unverified. The trace-store requirement does not require the RTX 4090.
Repository is unarchived and its default branch is main.
Latest default-branch commit was 83d152e18926d1e463c67aaf023647801ed14862 at 2026-10-02T00:01:57Z, within the 90-day window.
Latest release was langwatch-3.20.0, published at 2026-10-02T00:31:27Z, within the 90-day window.
GitHub API reported issue activity on 2026-10-01. This establishes activity, not response-time or resolution quality.
Local traces, spans and inspection are available without an enterprise license or a paid hosted service. Optional licensed features are not necessary for this requirement.

not_selected.name: OpenLIT
not_selected.reason: Close finalist: documents both client integrations, persistent local storage and OTLP HTTP/gRPC; its agent-hook fixtures and passing Go CI are strong evidence, but they do not establish superiority over LangWatch's native-client ingestion and local bootstrap. [Release README](https://github.com/openlit/openlit/blob/openlit-2.1.0/README.md), [Codex fixtures](https://github.com/openlit/openlit/blob/openlit-2.1.0/cli/internal/coding/hook/codex/handle_test.go), [passing CLI test job](https://github.com/openlit/openlit/actions/runs/36825597705/job/110250469651).

not_selected.name: MLflow
not_selected.reason: Close contender with a simple local server, SQLite persistence, OTLP/HTTP ingestion and Claude Code hooks; consolidating experiment tracking could favor it, but that benefit has not been measured for this packet and its inspected OTLP endpoint requires experiment routing. [Local start](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/5fb75a55ed41/README.md), [OTLP ingestion](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/5fb75a55ed41/docs/docs/genai/tracing/opentelemetry/ingest-shared.mdx), [Claude Code integration](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/5fb75a55ed41/docs/docs/genai/tracing/integrations/listing/claude_code.mdx).

not_selected.name: Jaeger
not_selected.reason: Strong generic OTLP trace-store control with passing unit and Badger storage tests; its inspected quickstart uses in-memory storage, while the selected project's client-specific session and conversation inspection more directly fits this layer. [Quickstart](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/e95545457675/README.md), [unit tests](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/actions/runs/36954903126/job/110675619946), [Badger tests](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/actions/runs/36954903126/job/110675620766).

not_selected.name: HyperDX / ClickStack
not_selected.reason: Credible local OTLP store with an all-in-one install, MCP access and passing OTLP smoke tests; its general observability scope adds no demonstrated advantage over the selected client's documented coding-session workflows for this requirement. [Installation](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/blob/b52adf718944/README.md), [MCP](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/blob/b52adf718944/MCP.md), [OTLP smoke job](https://github.com/hyperdxio/hyperdx/actions/runs/36920517517/job/110565115653).

not_selected.name: Opik
not_selected.reason: Strong local LLM tracing, evaluation and MCP capabilities with passing SDK and end-to-end tests; the inspected material does not provide a deciding comparison against the selected tool's explicit native telemetry setups for both clients. [Capabilities and local installation](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/blob/3de1c5e630ff/README.md), [SDK unit tests](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/actions/runs/36891099628/job/110466635732), [end-to-end tests](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/actions/runs/36891099668/job/110466634676).

not_selected.name: Langfuse
not_selected.reason: Capable self-hosted LLM observability platform; its documented Compose deployment has six services and offers no verified install or inspection advantage over the selected local bootstrap for this narrow requirement. Service count is not treated as a resource benchmark. [README](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/9a29212e855c/README.md), [Compose deployment](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/9a29212e855c/docker-compose.yml).

not_selected.reason: Maintained OpenTelemetry-native APM with trace inspection, MCP integration and passing Go tests; its broader infrastructure-observation capabilities do not establish a better fit than the selected client's specific LLM and coding-agent workflows. layers.deciding_comparison: The selection is a narrow capability-and-install preference, not a measured overall winner. Compare LangWatch, OpenLIT and MLflow on fresh WSL2 Ubuntu, with Jaeger as a generic OTLP control. Pin actual runtime artifacts and both client versions; ingest the same native OTLP output and fixed trace fixtures; measure preservation of trace IDs, parent links, events, token data and captured content, duplicate handling, fixed query and inspection tasks, restart persistence, cold-start time, ingestion/query latency, total CPU/RAM/disk use across every child service, and duplicated functionality or storage when experiment tracking is enabled. Keep workload and retention equal.
evidence_gaps: Judged as of 2026-10-02, with a 90-day cutoff of 2026-07-04. Repository metadata, default-branch commits, recent releases, issue activity and head check summaries were inspected for all ten candidates. All ten were unarchived; the nine retained candidates had recent default-branch commits and recent releases.

The packet contains no completed all-arm comparison. No public benchmark of the exact two-client WSL2 ingestion, inspection and resource workload was verified in the inspected sources. No throughput, latency, storage-cost or memory superiority is claimed.

LangWatch's inspected default-branch head had only a successful Mintlify Deployment check. Its application and packaged-install suite definitions were inspected, but a passing execution of those suites was not verified. The head's SUCCESS rollup therefore does not establish that the application tests passed.

Jaeger's inspected head had passing unit/storage/build checks but a failed Scorecard analysis check; it is not reported as entirely green. MLflow's inspected head listed unit and end-to-end checks as skipped, so those checks are not counted as passing.

No clean installation or live client export was run. Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 build/test targets support platform plausibility for the finalists; actual WSL2 and laptop operation remains unmeasured. Secondary-platform coverage for the other retained candidates was not verified in comparable depth.
The selected upstream npx command is unpinned. The GitHub source commit and release were verified, but the exact npm artifact version and runtime dependency digests were not independently verified.

OpenLIT's application release was recent, but the inspected published CLI release was cli-0.0.1 from 2026-06-10. Its repository remains maintained; compatibility of that downloaded CLI with the current client versions needs verification.

Correction during review: LangWatch's current README documents npx @langwatch/server with Node.js as the stated prerequisite. Its production Docker dependencies do not establish a disadvantage for the local quickstart. This correction was verified against the upstream README and packaged-install smoke workflow; the bootstrap command does not imply one process or lower RAM use.

The requested ctx_fetch_and_index route was blocked because the session's approval policy is never. Public upstream source files were instead retrieved through gh api, indexed with ctx_index and read with ctx_search. The web-search attempt failed with HTTP 502. Budget used: 30 GitHub API requests, three attempted search queries and one blocked page-fetch attempt. No local project file was opened beyond the supplied packet.
